history.dynasty: Sikh tradition (visits of Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Guru Har Gobind Sahib)
history.period: Guru Nanak's visit dated 15 Asu 1574 Bikrami (c. 1517 CE) in the Bhai Bala Janamsakhi
history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurdwara Manikaran Sahib commemorates the visit of Guru Nanak Dev Ji with Bhai Mardana during his third udasi (dated 15 Asu 1574 Bikrami in the Bhai Bala Janamsakhi), when a hot spring miraculously appeared to cook the langar - the same spring water still cooks the gurdwara's free langar today. Guru Har Gobind Sahib is also said to have visited. The gurdwara stands on the Parvati river amid the hot springs that Hindus associate with Shiva and Parvati's lost earring (mani), alongside older Hindu temples (Rama, Shiva). name: Gurdwara Sri Manikaran Sahib
town_description: Manikaran is a pilgrimage town in the Parvati Valley of Kullu district, at about 1,760 m on the banks of the Parvati river. Sacred to both Hindus and Sikhs for its hot springs, it hosts the historic gurdwara beside older Hindu temples, with pilgrims bathing in and cooking with the geothermal waters. The town lies ~45 km from Kullu and ~3 km from Kasol on the Bhuntar-Manikaran road.
